source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Lewisville DFW2 carries 12 MW of published IT capacity across 200,000 square feet, which is a minor contributor to Texas supply and modest by AI training standards.

The facility is one of 19 Texas sites with published capacity, and its 12 MW is 2.5 percent of the state's 475 MW of announced IT load, ranking 12th. Texas has 133 mapped data center sites, but most publish no capacity figure, so the state's real total is larger than the published number and this site's rank is a rank among the disclosing minority.

The certifications, PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, SSAE 16 Type II, and TIA-942, qualify the campus for regulated finance, healthcare, and government workloads rather than frontier AI training. At 40 kW per rack, the published capacity supports roughly 300 racks, a small footprint against current training cluster sizes.

What the data does not cover is decisive for AI: grid headroom in the Dallas, Fort Worth region and any announced expansion. The suitability score of 58 lists announced expansion as missing, so the score reflects only published capacity and operator type. A 12 MW facility can matter to AI if power is available and the operator can build beyond the published spec, and neither is disclosed here.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
